svg.title: A Halloween evening that welcomes everyone

text.tspan: A costume creates a playful Halloween character.
A Halloween evening that welcomes everyone
When we prepare a Halloween evening, a little care can make the experience better. Planning and
thinking about other people both help.
First, planning the route and the costumes helps everyone stay comfortable. For example, we check that
costumes allow clear vision and choose a well-lit route. This is a small thing that makes the day easier.
Second, clear choices make sharing treats more considerate. For example, we keep ingredient
information available and offer a non-food option. We do not need a perfect day to do this well.
We can prepare a Halloween evening more easily when we prepare and notice other people. These
simple steps give us a useful place to start.
BUILD YOUR OWN · State a focused main idea. Develop one supporting reason in each body paragraph, with a concrete
example. Conclude by connecting the two reasons without introducing a new argument. Use the structure as a model; write
about an experience of your own.
Look again. What two reasons support the main idea? Explain one example. (Model: The two reasons are that planning the
route and the costumes helps everyone stay comfortable and that clear choices make sharing treats more considerate. One
example is that we check that costumes allow clear vision and choose a well-lit route.)
